title: Attention Is All You Need
content: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
Google Brain · Google Research · University of Toronto
31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2017)
A new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
presenter_notes: Greet the audience and introduce this seminal work from NeurIPS 2017, which fundamentally changed how we approach sequence modeling by replacing RNNs with pure attention.

title: Background: Sequence Transduction is Fundamental to AI
content: Sequence transduction is the core engine behind Language Modeling and Machine Translation.
The field has been dominated by Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), specifically LSTMs and GRUs.
These models process data sequentially, maintaining a hidden state that evolves with each input symbol.
While effective, the sequential nature of these architectures creates a significant bottleneck for modern AI scaling.
presenter_notes: Start by framing the importance of sequence modeling. Explain that while RNNs were the gold standard, their sequential design is becoming a liability in the era of large-scale data.

title: The Problem: Sequential Computation Bottlenecks
content: Sequential processing prevents parallelization within training examples, leading to massive training times.
Memory constraints become critical for long sequences as the model must maintain a chain of hidden states.
Convolutional alternatives (e.g., ByteNet) attempt parallelization but struggle with long-range dependencies.
The computational cost to link distant positions grows with the distance between them, making it hard to learn global context.

title: Solution Overview: The Transformer Architecture
content: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations.
It eschews recurrence and convolution, allowing for significantly more parallelization.
The architecture follows a stacked encoder-decoder structure using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers.
This design achieves state-of-the-art results in a fraction of the training time.
presenter_notes: Introduce the high-level architecture. Point out the encoder on the left and the decoder on the right, emphasizing that every layer uses attention to look at the entire sequence at once.

title: Technical Detail: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
content: The core building block: Attention(Q, K, V).
Queries (Q) and Keys (K) of dimension $d_k$ are used to compute compatibility scores.
A scaling factor of $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ is applied to prevent the dot product from growing too large, which would lead to vanishing gradients in the softmax.
The final output is a weighted sum of the Values (V).

equation_reference.context: We compute the matrix of outputs as: Attention(Q, K, V ) = softmax(QKT / sqrt(dk))V

presenter_notes: Explain the mechanics of scaled dot-product attention. Emphasize why the scaling factor is crucial for training stability when the dimensionality is high.

title: Technical Detail: Multi-Head Attention
content: Instead of a single attention function, we perform attention $h$ times in parallel.
This allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
Each 'head' can focus on different types of relationships (e.g., one head for syntax, another for semantics).
The outputs are concatenated and projected to the final dimension.

presenter_notes: Explain that Multi-Head Attention is like having multiple 'filters' in a CNN, but for attention. It gives the model the power to capture complex, multi-faceted relationships in the data.

title: Technical Detail: Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks
content: Each layer in the encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network (FFN).
This FFN is applied to each position separately and identically.
It consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between.
While the linear transformations are the same across positions, they use different parameters from layer to layer.

equation_reference.context: In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully connected feed-forward network...

presenter_notes: The FFN provides the necessary non-linearity. Explain that while attention handles the 'mixing' of information across positions, the FFN processes the information within each position.

title: Technical Detail: Injecting Order via Positional Encodings
content: Since the model contains no recurrence or convolution, it has no inherent sense of sequence order.
We inject 'positional encodings' into the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.
We use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies.
This allows the model to learn to attend by relative positions, as for any fixed offset $k$, $PE_{pos+k}$ can be represented as a linear function of $PE_{pos}$.

equation_reference.latex:
P E(pos,2i) = sin(pos/100002i/dmodel)
P E(pos,2i+1) = cos(pos/100002i/dmodel)
equation_reference.context: In this work, we use sine and cosine functions of different frequencies...

presenter_notes: This is a clever solution to the 'bag-of-words' problem. Explain that these sinusoidal signals provide a unique signature for each position that the model can use to reconstruct the sequence order.

title: Experimental Setup: Machine Translation
content: Datasets: WMT 2014 English-to-German (4.5M sentence pairs) and English-to-French (36M sentence pairs).
Hardware: 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs.
Training: Base model trained for 100,000 steps (12 hours); Big model trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days).
Optimizer: Adam with a custom learning rate scheduler featuring a warmup phase.

title: Key Results: State-of-the-Art Translation Quality
content: The Transformer (big) achieves 28.4 BLEU on EN-DE, outperforming all previous models and ensembles by over 2.0 BLEU.
On EN-FR, it reaches 41.8 BLEU, setting a new single-model state-of-the-art.
Crucially, these results were achieved at a fraction of the training cost (FLOPs) of competing architectures like GNMT or ConvS2S.
Even the base model outperforms most previous ensembles.

presenter_notes: This is the 'hero' slide. Highlight the massive gap in training cost (FLOPs) while simultaneously achieving higher BLEU scores. This proves that attention is not just better, but more efficient.

title: Ablation Study: What Makes the Transformer Work?
content: Multi-head attention is superior to a single large head; performance drops as the number of heads decreases.
Reducing the attention key size $d_k$ hurts model quality, suggesting that compatibility is complex.
Larger models (higher $d_{model}$, $d_{ff}$) and stronger regularization (dropout) are key to reaching peak performance.
Sinusoidal positional encodings perform nearly identically to learned positional embeddings.

presenter_notes: Discuss the ablation results. Point out that the 'Multi-Head' aspect is not just a gimmick—it's essential for performance. Also, note that the model scales very well with size.

title: Generalization: English Constituency Parsing
content: To test if the Transformer generalizes beyond translation, we applied it to English constituency parsing.
Despite being a task with strong structural constraints, the Transformer achieved competitive results.
In a semi-supervised setting, it achieved 92.7 F1, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models.
This demonstrates that the attention mechanism is capable of learning task-specific structures without explicit inductive biases.

title: Visualizing Attention: Capturing Structure
content: Attention heads learn to perform distinct tasks related to the syntactic and semantic structure of the sentence.
Some heads focus on long-distance dependencies, linking words across the entire sentence.
Other heads specialize in anaphora resolution, correctly linking pronouns to their referents.
This visualization provides interpretability, showing how the model 'understands' the input.
presenter_notes: Use the visualization to show the 'magic' under the hood. Explain that different heads are looking for different things, which is why the multi-head approach is so powerful.

title: Conclusion & Impact
content: The Transformer proves that 'Attention Is All You Need' for high-performance sequence modeling.
It replaces slow, sequential RNNs with a fast, parallelizable architecture.
Achieved new SOTA results in translation and parsing with significantly lower training costs.
This work laid the foundation for the current era of Large Language Models (LLMs).
presenter_notes: Summarize the core message. The Transformer didn't just improve translation; it changed the fundamental architecture of AI, enabling the massive scaling we see today.

title: Future Work & Broader Significance
content: Applying the Transformer to non-text modalities: images, audio, and video.
Investigating local, restricted attention mechanisms to handle even longer sequences efficiently.
Optimizing the generation process to be less sequential (non-autoregressive decoding).
The architecture's scalability suggests it will be the backbone of future large-scale AI systems.
